answer_sql:
WITH german AS (
  SELECT
    'store' AS reading,
    l.order_date,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON l.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON s.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name = 'Germany'
    AND l.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND l.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'customer',
    l.order_date,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS cu
    ON l.customer_key = cu.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON cu.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name = 'Germany'
    AND l.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND l.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  STRFTIME(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', order_date), '%Y-%m') AS month,
  ROUND(SUM(net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
    reading = 'store'), 2) AS revenue_german_stores,
  ROUND(SUM(net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
    reading = 'customer'), 2) AS revenue_german_customers
FROM german
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  month ASC

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: Twelve rows, one per month of calendar 2024 in order, each carrying the same quantity measured two ways: the money Contoso actually charged after discount, in USD, on orders placed in that month that count as German. `revenue_german_stores` is what premises located in Germany rang up — 1,812 order lines, 1,540,736.67 across the year, containing no internet sales whatsoever, because the web shop's store country is the '--' sentinel the declarations state is not a place. `revenue_german_customers` is what people resident in Germany spent wherever they bought — 4,717 order lines, 3,969,307.19 across the year, of which 2,428,570.52 is the web shop. The two columns must not be added: they overlap on the 1,812 lines that are German both ways, and measurement showed that in 2024 no German shop sold to a foreigner and no German customer bought at a foreign shop, so the web shop is the whole of the disagreement. Every one of the 12 monthly pairs matches the independently-read series from the aggregation step, so the figures are confirmed and not sampled. What I did NOT include in either column: gross revenue before discount, any currency conversion (these are USD, not EUR, whatever currency each sale was transacted in), any other country, any other year, orders dated by delivery rather than by order, and any month-over-month or 2023 comparison.

value:
Which Germany do you mean — what your German shops took, or what your German customers spent? The choice changes 2024 by 2.6x, so I have not picked for you. Both full series, measured:

(a) "Revenue booked by the German stores" — the shops standing in Germany, 1,540,736.67 net USD for 2024, all of it walk-in trade: Jan 183,331.42, Feb 148,576.18, Mar 142,393.47, Apr 62,471.08, May 179,682.27, Jun 130,040.27, Jul 89,958.42, Aug 82,736.15, Sep 75,772.92, Oct 122,211.15, Nov 168,054.81, Dec 155,508.54.

(b) "Revenue from customers based in Germany" — people resident in Germany, wherever they bought, 3,969,307.19 net USD for 2024: Jan 462,130.58, Feb 425,189.58, Mar 266,907.74, Apr 163,417.57, May 380,687.75, Jun 299,707.59, Jul 186,061.91, Aug 339,079.19, Sep 267,042.45, Oct 369,463.94, Nov 450,137.80, Dec 359,481.10.

Tell me which and the answer is the 12 figures under it, unchanged — nothing needs recomputing.

The entire 2,428,570.52 difference is German customers ordering from the web shop. The web shop has no country of its own in this data, so reading (a) cannot see those sales at all — it is not that they are small, it is that the route cannot reach them.

It changes more than the level. Under (a) August is the year's third-weakest month; under (b) it is the fourth-strongest. If you are asking whether Germany softened in late summer, the two readings answer oppositely.

What the choice does NOT change: all 12 months carry sales either way, so no month is missing or shown as a zero the data did not supply; January is the strongest month and April the weakest under both; and the figures are net of discount in USD, dated by order date, on calendar 2024 — dating by delivery instead moves (b) by 1,385.10 and (a) by nothing at all.

Your third possible reading, orders SHIPPED to Germany, I cannot give you: this bundle records a delivery date but no delivery address.

Two populations, both reported in full, neither chosen. (a) All sales lines whose selling store's country is Germany with order_date in 2024-01-01..2024-12-31: 1,812 lines. Physical-only by construction rather than by any filter I applied — the web shop carries '--' as its store country, so no internet line can qualify. (b) All sales lines whose customer's country of residence is Germany, same window: 4,717 lines, spanning both channels. Both columns: net of discount, in USD, grouped to month on order_date, no channel predicate, and no store trading-state predicate — so shops that have since closed are included in the months they actually traded. The third declared route, site country via dim_location, was measured and returns byte-identical rows to (a) (14,190 lines, 14,382,768.44 all-time), so it is not a separate reading in this bundle. Excluded from both: every other country, every other year, and the 'shipped to Germany' reading, which no column here can express.

WITH german AS (
  SELECT
    'store' AS reading,
    l.order_date,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON l.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON s.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name = 'Germany'
    AND l.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND l.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'customer',
    l.order_date,
    l.net_amount
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS cu
    ON l.customer_key = cu.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS c
    ON cu.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE
    c.country_name = 'Germany'
    AND l.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND l.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  STRFTIME(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', order_date), '%Y-%m') AS month,
  ROUND(SUM(net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
    reading = 'store'), 2) AS revenue_german_stores,
  ROUND(SUM(net_amount) FILTER(WHERE
    reading = 'customer'), 2) AS revenue_german_customers
FROM german
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  month ASC
value.means: Twelve rows, one per month of calendar 2024 in order, each carrying the same quantity measured two ways: the money Contoso actually charged after discount, in USD, on orders placed in that month that count as German. `revenue_german_stores` is what premises located in Germany rang up — 1,812 order lines, 1,540,736.67 across the year, containing no internet sales whatsoever, because the web shop's store country is the '--' sentinel the declarations state is not a place. `revenue_german_customers` is what people resident in Germany spent wherever they bought — 4,717 order lines, 3,969,307.19 across the year, of which 2,428,570.52 is the web shop. The two columns must not be added: they overlap on the 1,812 lines that are German both ways, and measurement showed that in 2024 no German shop sold to a foreigner and no German customer bought at a foreign shop, so the web shop is the whole of the disagreement. Every one of the 12 monthly pairs matches the independently-read series from the aggregation step, so the figures are confirmed and not sampled. What I did NOT include in either column: gross revenue before discount, any currency conversion (these are USD, not EUR, whatever currency each sale was transacted in), any other country, any other year, orders dated by delivery rather than by order, and any month-over-month or 2023 comparison.

readings.took: NEITHER reading — the choice is handed back priced, because the two give 1,540,736.67 and 3,969,307.19 for 2024 and also disagree about the shape of the second half of the year. The returned rows cannot resolve this: they report both columns, which is the fork and not its answer
readings.could_also_mean: revenue booked by the German shops (a), or revenue from customers resident in Germany (b); the 2,428,570.52 gap is entirely German customers buying from the web shop
readings.declaration: country.default.whose_country_is_asked_never_assumed (confidence C, operator ruling 2026-10-22) — 'never: pick between the store and the customer silently, and never average the two'. It declares store, customer and location paths and deliberately names NO default. The decomposition had assumed Germany would be attributed 'however your data normally attributes country'; this bundle's answer is that it has no normal way, which is exactly why the rule exists

readings.took: reported as inexpressible rather than answered or silently dropped
readings.could_also_mean: orders shipped to a German address — but the sales line carries delivery_date and no delivery country, state or city, so there is no ship-to geography in this bundle at all
readings.declaration: v_contoso5_sales_line declares delivery_date only; the sole routes from a sale to a place are the store's country and the customer's country of residence

readings.took: net_amount — what the customer was actually charged, after discount, in USD. Both series are NET
readings.could_also_mean: gross revenue as invoiced, before discount — a different question rather than another route to this one; across the whole bundle that gap is 13,787,071.00
readings.declaration: net_revenue.default.revenue_means_net (P): answer on net_amount and say NET — 'the gap between net and gross is the discount'

readings.took: no channel predicate — (b) therefore spans shop and web, and (a) excludes the web only because that route cannot reach it
readings.could_also_mean: physical shops only, which for (b) would give 1,540,736.67 — identical to (a), since in 2024 every German customer's in-shop purchase was at a German shop
readings.declaration: store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel carries `applies: subject`, so its `physical` default reaches questions whose subject is a Store, not a measure; the operator's 2026-10-18 ruling puts unqualified revenue across both channels

readings.took: calendar year on order_date, 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31, with orders present at both edges of the window
readings.could_also_mean: a fiscal 2024, which this bundle cannot express — no fiscal calendar or year-offset is declared anywhere
readings.declaration: order.default.period_is_order_date (P); order_date carries `period_binding: True`

readings.took: order_date — with the alternative priced rather than merely declared away: by delivery_date (b) becomes 3,970,692.29, 0.03% apart, and (a) is identical to the cent
readings.could_also_mean: delivery_date; the invoice-date and revenue-recognition-date readings have no column in this bundle
readings.declaration: order.default.period_is_order_date (P): 'Order date is the reporting convention; delivery is a logistics question'

readings.took: USD — the unit the amounts are stored in on every line, whatever currency the sale was transacted in
readings.could_also_mean: EUR, which a reader asking about Germany might well expect; that needs per-line conversion through ExchangeRate at each order date and was not asked for
readings.declaration: currency.ambiguity.code_is_not_the_unit_of_the_amounts: never present the USD amounts as if they were in that currency

readings.took: the 12 monthly figures in calendar order, nothing added
readings.could_also_mean: the figures plus month-over-month change, or 2024 beside the same months of 2023 — both are extra columns on this table, so neither would change the figures given
readings.declaration: nothing declared; kept to the decomposition's reading
